Traditional semiconductor packaging faces reliability risks, such as material stress and delamination, caused by mismatches in the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) among different materials during heating. The passage details methods for manufacturing multi-chip modules (MCMs) and super-large integrated fan-out (InFO) package components (greater than 70 mm by 70 mm) suitable for high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) applications. 

The manufacturing process begins by fabricating and testing interconnect structures—which include substrates, dielectric layers, metallization layers, redistribution layers, and through-substrate vias (TSVs)—to ensure only known good components are used. These tested structures (either as a plurality of discrete semi-finished substrates or a single universal interconnect structure) are bonded to a carrier substrate using an adhesive film. A first encapsulant is applied and cured around the interconnect structures, then thinned (e.g., via chemical mechanical polishing) to create a planar reconstructed wafer with exposed external connectors. 

In some embodiments, tested packaged semiconductor devices (such as processors and memory cubes with InFO layers) are aligned and bonded directly to the exposed connectors of the reconstructed wafer. The devices can be arranged over individual interconnect structures, bridge adjacent structures, or share a single universal interconnect structure. Bonding is achieved via solder bonding or low-temperature direct copper-to-copper (Cu-to-Cu) bonding. 

In other embodiments, a series of universal redistribution layers (URDLs) comprising patterned dielectric and conductive layers are formed over the reconstructed wafer first. A passivation layer and device connections (including under-bump metallizations and contact bumps) are formed over the URDLs, and discrete semiconductor components are subsequently flip-chip bonded to these connections.

Following component attachment, an underfill material (such as capillary underfill or moldable underfill) is applied between the semiconductor components and the underlying surface to reduce stress and protect the bonds. The semiconductor components and portions of the first encapsulant are then encased in a second encapsulant, which is cured and thinned to expose the backsides of the devices. Finally, the carrier substrate is de-bonded using a thermal process (such as laser irradiation) to alter the adhesive, and external connections (e.g., solder bumps or conductive pillars) are formed on the exposed side of the interconnect structures. 

Integrating this process in wafer form simplifies manufacturing, while pre-testing components, utilizing low-temperature Cu-to-Cu bonding, and matching the CTE of the package to that of a printed circuit board (PCB) minimizes material stress and significantly improves component-level and board-level reliability.

This patent application, which is a continuation of several prior applications dating back to 2015, discloses a tonneau cover designed to create a secure compartment over a pickup truck bed. The cover consists of a stationary base panel attached to the truck's opposing side walls and multiple movable panel sections that pivot via hinge assemblies to allow access to the bed. 

Each movable panel section is secured and released from the truck's side walls using its own latching assembly fitted flush into the panel's underside frame. A latching assembly comprises two opposing, spring-loaded pinch latch assemblies located adjacent to the respective side walls and linked together by a longitudinally extending connector (such as a panel, bar, or rod). Each pinch latch assembly includes a stationary latch guide, a latch handle portion (containing a latch, spring pockets, springs, and guide tabs), and an inner pinch handle portion (containing a handle and slots to receive the guide tabs). The springs bias the latches into an extended, latched condition where they engage adjustable clips mounted on side rails. When an operator pinches the handles of one assembly together against the spring resistance, the latch on that side retracts. Simultaneously, the movement pulls the longitudinal connector, which actuates the opposing inner pinch handle and retracts the opposite latch. Consequently, an operator can unlatch both sides of a panel section from just one side of the truck. Releasing the handles allows the springs to automatically return both latches to the latched condition. The inner pinch handles may also feature a cavity to hold a removable light to illuminate the truck bed, and spring tabs to minimize vibration and noise while the vehicle is moving.

The tonneau cover incorporates several additional structural and weatherproofing features:
*   **Side Rails:** The cover rests on side rails fastened to the truck bed walls using adjustable brackets and clamps. The rails feature a logistic track to hold the latch-receiving clips and a D-shaped seal to prevent water from entering the bed. The rearmost panel section also includes a flange edge with a gasket seal to block water at the tailgate seam.
*   **Hinge Assemblies:** The panels are connected by hinge assemblies featuring opposing hinge brackets, a resilient rubber or silicone hinge seal, a hinge seal spacer, and hinge seal rods. These components allow the panels to fold flat over one another while maintaining separation, friction, and weather sealing.
*   **Vertical Support Gusset Assembly:** When the panels are folded and raised into a vertical stowed position to uncover the bed, they can be supported by a gusset assembly. The gusset has a lower end with a ball/pivot joint that slides into the side rail's logistic track and an upper aperture that receives the panel's spring-loaded latch. When not in use, the gusset pivots downward to stow underneath the panels, supported by a rail clip, or can be removed entirely.
*   **Securement System:** To further secure the folded panels in the upright position, a channel bracket is affixed to the base panel. This bracket holds the folded panels upright and off the base panel's surface to prevent scratching. A buckle strap attached near the latching assembly snaps into a buckle receptacle to prevent the panels from bouncing or pivoting into the truck cab. The buckle system can also secure the panels when they are folded in a horizontal position to prevent them from unfolding due to wind while the truck is moving.

Developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, Bollinger Bands are a technical analysis indicator used to visualize asset volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a central moving average (defaulting to 20 periods) with upper and lower bands calculated by adding and subtracting a multiple of the standard deviation. 

While useful for creating trading systems, Bollinger Bands alone do not guarantee profitability. Their disadvantages include false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, signal delays due to reliance on historical data, and sensitivity to setting adjustments. 

On the TradingView platform, users can customize the moving average length, standard deviation values, and data source, or calculate the bands using Pine Script's `ta.sma()` and `ta.stedv()` functions. Ultimately, the indicator's effectiveness depends on defining proper trading rules, managing risk, and backtesting across different timeframes to build strategies such as Breakout, Mean Reversion, or Squeeze.

Created and refined by Tex Winter, the Triangle Post Offense is a basketball system that relies on defensive recognition rather than set plays. It is based on sound principles, executing fundamentals, and precise 15-to-20-foot court spacing to spread the defense, discourage double-teaming, and allow for sharp passing and one-on-one play. The offense consists of three main components: the Entry, a sideline triangle on one side of the court, and a two-man game on the weakside. 

The offense can be initiated through numerous pass or dribble entries—such as guard cuts, dribble clears, post pops, screens, and ball reversals—making it difficult for defenses to disrupt. Once established, the sideline triangle creates strong one-on-one post-ups and quick-hitting post split options, including basic splits, high splits, isolations, and screen-and-rolls. Two-player post solo cuts can also be used instead of the triangle.

A reversal pass to the off-guard initiates the weakside "Two Game" via a pass or dribble series. Because offensive options are entirely dictated by defensive deployment, players must read the defense to execute specific counters, such as driving, pulling up for a jumper, rolling, or cutting opposite. Additionally, the system features automatic counters when the defense attempts to deny passing lanes, front or double-team the post, sag off, or trap. 

Successfully building this offense requires teaching through breakdown drills (progressing from 2-on-2 to 5-on-5), focusing on individual skill development during practice, and scouting opponents to prepare for defensive adjustments. Because it is one of the most used offenses, teams must also learn how to defend against it.

Plaintiff Paula Norrell brought a federal action against Defendant Waste Away Group, Inc., alleging unlawful gender discrimination under Title VII, specifically claiming a failure to promote (disparate treatment) and employment practices causing a disparate impact. Defendant filed a Motion for Summary Judgment.

Norrell was hired by Waste Away in 1996 and received promotions and raises, eventually becoming the Opelika district sales manager in 1998. In 2001, Waste Away combined the Montgomery and Opelika sales districts. Division managers Jeff Johnson and Mike Mitchell interviewed three candidates for the combined district sales manager position: Norrell, Greg Folmar, and Terry White. They selected White, a male who had previously held the exact combined district sales manager position. Waste Away offered Norrell a reinstated Temporary Construction Representative position at a slightly lower salary. After taking maternity leave, Norrell declined the offer and left the company.

In analyzing the disparate treatment claim under the *McDonnell Douglas* framework, the court found that Norrell established a prima facie case of sex discrimination (applying the *Walker* standard, which does not require proving relative qualifications at the prima facie stage). Waste Away then met its burden by articulating a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for promoting White: he was the most qualified candidate, possessing prior experience in the exact combined role, outside sales experience, and strong leadership skills, whereas Norrell lacked outside sales experience, required involved supervision, and had limited knowledge of the Montgomery sales market.

The burden shifted back to Norrell to prove Waste Away's reasons were a pretext for discrimination. Norrell argued that: (1) her supervisor, Mike Malphrus, asked her to train White; (2) Malphrus made discriminatory remarks about women and influenced the decision; and (3) Johnson made a crude comment about his own wife's pregnancy. The court rejected these arguments, finding that Norrell never actually trained White—who already had experience in the role—and that Norrell failed to prove she was substantially more qualified than White. Furthermore, Malphrus was not a decisionmaker in the promotion, Johnson and Mitchell conducted an independent review of the candidates, and the alleged remarks by Malphrus and Johnson were isolated, stray remarks unrelated to the decisional process. 

Additionally, Norrell conceded after discovery that she did not have a claim for disparate impact discrimination. Consequently, the court granted Waste Away’s Motion for Summary Judgment on all claims, entered final judgment in favor of the Defendant, and taxed costs against the Plaintiff.

The double top chart pattern is a bearish reversal formation occurring at the end of an uptrend or a prolonged pullback in a downtrend. It consists of two swing highs ending around the same resistance level (within 3% of each other) and a swing low between them. Connecting the swing low to the preceding swing low forms a support level called the neckline. 

When the price breaks below the neckline on significant volume, it signals a likely downward price movement. Consequently, traders may close long positions or open short positions upon the break or a neckline retest. Profit targets are estimated by projecting the pattern's height downward from the neckline, while stop losses are placed in the middle of or above the pattern.

Coding and backtesting this pattern is difficult and time-consuming. Research by Thomas Bulkowski, who manually analyzed 500 stocks over five years, found that only 39% of double top formations reach their target, compared to 68% for double bottoms. Because the stock market has an upward tailwind from inflation and increased productivity, shorting is generally difficult, making the double top a tough formation to trade.

Following the death of primatologist Jane Goodall on October 1 at age 91, the author recalls a 1990 interview regarding her collection of chimpanzee skeletons from Tanzania’s Gombe National Park. Believing nothing in the field should be wasted, Goodall and her team preserved the bones of chimps whose sex, age, weight, and life experiences were already documented. Unlike ancient hominid fossils from unknown individuals, these skeletons allowed researchers to study how an individual's life journey impacts bone development. Though Goodall was humble about the collection's implications for ancient hominids, the bones yielded significant insights. For instance, the skeleton of a matriarch named Flo demonstrated the difficulty of estimating body weight from bone size and showed a bone loss pattern distinct from human osteoporosis, aligning with observations of her late-life fertility. Ultimately, Goodall's skeletal collection provided enduring scientific value regarding skeletal formation.

Developed by William J. O’Neil, a follow-through day is a market-timing concept used to identify the transition from a market correction or downtrend to a new uptrend. It begins with a rally attempt after a market bottom, where Day 1 is marked by a major index closing higher than the previous day (or closing slightly down in the top half of the day's range). For the rally attempt to remain valid, the index must not fall below its recent low on Days 2 and 3. The follow-through day occurs on Day 4 or later (typically Days 4 to 7) when a major index closes significantly higher with greater volume than the preceding day. If the index subsequently falls below the initial low, the signal has completely failed.

While no bull market since the early 1900s has started without a follow-through day, the signal is not perfect and does not always indicate the absolute bottom. Furthermore, backtesting the strategy on the S&P 500 (using the SPY ETF) yields poor short-term results because the market has been mean-revertive over the last three decades, making it better to buy on weakness rather than strength. However, results improve slightly when adding a 25-day RSI filter, and results might differ on individual stocks, which were O'Neil's actual focus. Consequently, the passage concludes that follow-through days are not particularly useful for short-term index traders.

This email from Courtney Votaw compiles news articles from October 28–29, 2001, detailing Enron Corp.'s financial difficulties and market impact.

**Financial and Credit Status**
Enron's stock fell to near seven-year lows (around $13.55 to $14.02), losing over half its value in two weeks following a reported $618 million to $638 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in charges, and a $1.2 billion equity write-down. These losses were linked to previously undisclosed partnerships managed by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow, who was subsequently ousted. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) launched an inquiry into the transactions. Consequently, Moody's Investors Service downgraded Enron's senior unsecured long-term debt from Baa1 to Baa2, placed its long-term debt and P-2 commercial paper ratings on review for further downgrade, and lowered ratings on two related trusts, Marlin and Osprey. Standard & Poor's and Fitch maintained BBB-plus ratings with negative outlooks. 

**Liquidity and Operations**
To boost investor confidence and pay off $2 billion in commercial paper, Enron tapped roughly $3 billion to $3.3 billion from existing credit lines and entered negotiations with banks, including Citigroup and J.P. Morgan Chase, for an additional $1 billion to $2 billion. Analysts noted that lenders will likely demand harsher terms and collateral, and viewed the credit drawdowns as a sign of desperation, though GimmeCredit stated a junk rating was unlikely. Enron also plans to reduce debt via a $2.9 billion sale of Portland General Electric and other asset sales. While U.S. energy traders like Mirant, El Paso, AEP, and Duke Energy reported normal trading levels with Enron while monitoring the situation, several large European energy groups froze dealings due to credit concerns. Additionally, a newsletter reported that Royal Dutch/Shell Group might consider a buyout of Enron.

**Broader Market and Community Context**
Rating agencies Moody's and S&P reported a broad decline in U.S. corporate credit quality, projecting $100 billion in defaults for the year amid a recession worsened by the September 11 attacks. Commentators noted that Enron's turmoil threatens overall market confidence. Another analysis highlighted positive insider buying at rival independent power producers (Calpine, AES, Mirant, and NRG Energy), contrasting this with consistent insider selling at Enron prior to its decline. Conversely, a *Houston Chronicle* opinion piece by Bill White praised Enron and Chairman Ken Lay for their innovation, economic revitalization of Houston, and extensive civic and charitable contributions, urging the public to support the company.

Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral disease that has become a significant public health concern in Ethiopia since its first detection in June 2016. With no approved vaccine or antiviral therapy available, disease management relies on symptom alleviation, vector control, and public awareness. Because the current epidemiological status of the disease in Ethiopia is unclear, this systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to determine the pooled seroprevalence of Chikungunya and provide insights for control and prevention strategies.

Following PRISMA guidelines, researchers searched multiple electronic databases for English-language observational studies on Chikungunya in Ethiopia published between 2016 and November 2023. Out of 40 identified publications, five studies (four cross-sectional and one case-control) encompassing five regional states and one city administration met the eligibility criteria. These studies utilized either ELISA (80%) or RT-qPCR (20%) for laboratory confirmation. 

The meta-analysis revealed a pooled Chikungunya seroprevalence of 12.35% in Ethiopia. Prevalence varied significantly by geographic location: the highest regional prevalence was in the Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region (43.6%), and the lowest was in Dire Dawa (approximately 12%). At the district level, Debub Ari had the highest prevalence (51.58%), while Lare had the lowest (6.25%). 

Furthermore, seroprevalence varied based on demographic factors. Farmers, adults, and individuals with formal education generally exhibited higher infection rates compared to other occupational, age, and educational groups. Findings regarding sex were inconsistent across the evaluated studies, with some reporting higher rates in males and others in females. Subgroup analyses indicated significant heterogeneity among districts and between diagnostic test types, with ELISA showing high variability across studies and RT-qPCR showing none. Statistical tests indicated no publication bias or small-study effects. 

While this study is the first to report the pooled seroprevalence of Chikungunya in Ethiopia, it is limited by the small number of eligible studies, a reliance on cross-sectional data, and a lack of molecular studies to predict circulating viral strains. The findings highlight that Chikungunya remains a persistent health concern in Ethiopia, necessitating proactive operational readiness, collaboration, and public awareness campaigns by the Ministry of Health and other concerned authorities.

During Monday's oral arguments, several Supreme Court justices appeared willing to let trial courts prohibit defense lawyers from directly discussing a client's ongoing testimony during overnight recesses, while still permitting discussions about related trial strategy. The case involves David Villarreal, who was convicted of murder after a judge barred his lawyer from discussing his testimony overnight, an order upheld by Texas courts. Villarreal's attorney argued this restriction violates the Sixth Amendment because the blurred line between strategy and testimony forces lawyers to self-censor. However, several justices believed a distinction could be drawn. If the Court permits such limits, it must choose between Texas's proposal—banning the "management" of testimony, including its content and delivery, while allowing strategic discussions—and the United States' proposed bright-line rule prohibiting any discussion of the testimony itself, though still allowing strategy advice like pursuing a plea bargain.

Developed by Stanford professor Joseph Piotroski, the Piotroski F-Score is a popular, systematic stock selection method used to identify undervalued and growth stocks with strong fundamentals. The strategy evaluates a company's financial health using nine criteria—including profitability, liquidity, and efficiency—assigning 1 or 0 to each. Scores of 8 or 9 indicate strong financials likely to outperform the market, whereas scores of 0 to 4 indicate poor financials. While effective for maximizing returns, reducing risk, and diversifying portfolios, it does not guarantee success and should be combined with additional research, regular monitoring, and historical backtesting. 

Empirical tests support the strategy. Alpha Architect backtested NYSE stocks (1974–2014) scoring at least 6, finding annual returns of 12.6% for the original score and 13.3% for their modified version, both beating the S&P 500’s 11.2%. When applied to the 20% cheapest stocks scoring above 6, returns rose to 15.2% (original) and 15.9% (modified). The score was also tested on European stocks by ValueSignals (1999–2011) and on Norwegian and Swedish stocks by Alexander Eriksen (1997–2011). Finally, the blog offers compiled packages of backtestable trading rules from its 1,200+ articles for purchase.

Modern applications require high availability, reliability, and scalability, necessitating the use of distributed systems. Containers and container orchestrators, like Kubernetes, provide the foundational building blocks for these systems by enabling the creation of reusable components and design patterns. Patterns offer a shared language, allow developers to learn from past mistakes, and facilitate the creation of modular components. 

Container patterns are divided into single-node and multi-node patterns. Splitting an application on a single machine into multiple co-scheduled containers (such as a Kubernetes pod) provides resource isolation, clear team ownership, and separation of concerns. To ensure these containers are modular and reusable, developers must parameterize them, clearly define their APIs, and document their operations.

There are three primary single-node patterns:
1. **The Sidecar Pattern:** A sidecar container is paired with a main application container to augment and extend its functionality without modifying the core application. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy web service, dynamically synchronizing configuration files, deploying process-monitoring utilities (like a `topz` interface), and syncing code from a Git repository to build a simple Platform as a Service (PaaS).
2. **The Ambassador Pattern:** An ambassador container acts as a proxy that brokers interactions between the application container and the external world. The application connects to the ambassador on `localhost`, while the ambassador handles complex logic such as routing requests to a sharded storage service (like Redis via twemproxy), brokering service discovery across different environments, or splitting traffic to run production experiments (such as routing 10% of traffic to a beta version using nginx).
3. **The Adapter Pattern:** An adapter container modifies the heterogeneous interfaces of various application containers to present a single, consistent interface to the outside world. This is widely used for standardizing application monitoring (e.g., exporting Redis metrics to Prometheus), normalizing different logging formats (e.g., using fluentd to capture slow query logs), and executing rich health-check scripts against databases like MySQL.

Multi-node distributed patterns are more loosely coupled and form the basis of microservices architectures. Microservices break applications into independent components that communicate over defined APIs, allowing small teams to build, maintain, and scale services independently, though they can be harder to debug and architect than monolithic systems.

Two key multi-node patterns are:
1. **Replicated Load-Balanced Services:** Used for stateless services, this pattern places multiple identical servers behind a load balancer for redundancy and horizontal scaling. It relies on readiness probes to confirm containers are ready to serve traffic, and can use session tracking (via IP hashing or cookies) to route a specific user's requests to the same replica. This pattern can be expanded by adding a replicated caching layer (like Varnish) to improve performance and implement rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, as well as an edge layer (like nginx) to handle SSL termination.
2. **Sharded Services:** Used for stateful services where the data is too large for a single machine, sharding splits the service so each shard only handles a subset of requests, directed by a load-balancing root node. A sharded cache sits between user requests and the frontend to increase the total size of data stored in the cache.

Containerization establishes boundaries for resource isolation, team ownership, and separation of concerns, motivating the division of single-node and distributed applications into modular, reusable containers. 

**Single-Node Patterns**
Tightly coupled containers scheduled onto a single machine (e.g., Kubernetes pods) share local resources like filesystems and networks. To ensure modularity and reusability, these containers should be parameterized, maintain a stable API, and be documented in their Dockerfile. There are three primary single-node patterns:
*   **Sidecar Pattern:** A sidecar container augments and extends a primary application container. Use cases include adding HTTPS to legacy services, dynamic configuration synchronization, process monitoring (e.g., topz), and building a Git-based PaaS. 
*   **Ambassador Pattern:** An ambassador container proxies network interactions between the application container and the external world. It is used for client-side routing to sharded storage (e.g., Redis via twemproxy), service discovery brokering across environments, and request splitting for experimentation.
*   **Adapter Pattern:** An adapter container modifies the heterogeneous interfaces of various application containers to present a single, consistent interface to external tools. Examples include adapting metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and running custom database health checks (e.g., for MySQL).

**Multi-Node Distributed Patterns**
Loosely coupled microservices run in separate processes and communicate over network APIs. While harder to debug and architect than monoliths, microservices allow small teams to independently manage, deploy, and scale components. Common distributed patterns include:
*   **Replicated Load-Balanced Services:** Identical, stateless servers placed behind a load balancer provide horizontal scaling, redundancy, and high availability. These architectures require readiness probes to verify initialization before serving traffic and can use IP hashing or cookies for session tracking. The pattern can be expanded with additional replicated layers: a caching proxy tier (e.g., Varnish) to improve performance and provide rate-limiting (denial-of-service defense), and an edge tier (e.g., nginx) for SSL termination.
*   **Sharded Services:** Used for stateful services when data is too large for a single machine. Each shard serves a unique subset of requests, maximizing memory utilization (e.g., in a sharded Memcache). Because losing a shard degrades performance by reducing the cache hit rate and increasing latency, shards can also be replicated to tolerate failures and handle high loads. Traffic is routed to shards via an ambassador or a shared routing service using a deterministic, uniform sharding function based on a specific request key. To prevent massive cache misses when scaling the number of shards, consistent hashing functions are used to minimize key remapping.

The TPS7H500x-SP series is a family of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak current mode PWM controllers designed for space-grade DC-DC converters using silicon or GaN power devices. The series operates from a 4-V to 14-V input supply, features a 0.613-V (+0.7%/-1% accurate) internal voltage reference, and supports switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. The switching frequency can be set using an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or a primary-secondary configuration for synchronizing or interleaving two controllers. 

The family consists of four devices tailored for various topologies, including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge:
*   **TPS7H5001-SP:** A full-featured, dual-output controller with integrated synchronous rectifier (SR) outputs, programmable dead time, programmable leading-edge blanking (LEB) time, and configurable maximum duty cycles (50%, 75%, or 100%).
*   **TPS7H5002-SP:** A single-output controller with an integrated SR output, configurable dead time and LEB time, and a 75% or 100% maximum duty cycle.
*   **TPS7H5003-SP:** A single-output controller with an integrated SR output, fixed 50-ns dead time and LEB time, and a 75% or 100% maximum duty cycle.
*   **TPS7H5004-SP:** A dual-output controller for non-synchronous topologies with configurable LEB time and a fixed 50% maximum duty cycle.

Because the primary and SR outputs have a peak current capability of roughly 150 mA, external gate drivers are recommended. Operational and protection features include adjustable undervoltage lockout (UVLO) via the EN pin, capacitor-programmable soft-start, a transconductance error amplifier supporting Type 2A or 2B compensation, programmable slope compensation, and a pulse-skipping mode to prevent inductor current runaway during high-frequency operation. For fault handling, the controllers feature cycle-by-cycle current limiting, capacitor-programmable hiccup mode for overcurrent protection, an external FAULT pin for custom shutdown triggers, and thermal shutdown at 175°C (restarting at 160°C).

The passage also details a design example for a 500-kHz, 5-V output synchronous push-pull converter using the TPS7H5001-SP and GaN FETs. This example provides calculations for selecting resistors, capacitors, the transformer, FET ratings, an RCD clamp, output inductors, and compensation networks. Finally, PCB layout guidelines are provided to minimize noise coupling, parasitic capacitance, and EMI—such as separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high dv/dt and di/dt loop areas, and placing bypass components close to the controller—alongside documentation references, revision history, and packaging disclaimers.

Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund, Danantara, will finance and oversee the launch of at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October. Starting in Jakarta and eventually expanding to 33 municipalities across Java and Bali, the initiative aims to boost renewable energy and help manage Indonesia's 35 million tonnes of annual waste. Each facility will cost roughly 2 trillion to 3 trillion rupiah (around $180 million) and process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily to generate 15 megawatts of electricity. State utility PLN will purchase the power for the national grid, while the government will support the rollout by removing municipal tipping fees and providing land. The program aligns with Indonesia's 2025–2034 electricity plan and Danantara's goals of generating financial returns while reducing pollution and landfill reliance.

Despite heightened political polarization and challenges following COVID-19 and the 2020 racial reckoning, states are successfully enacting substantive "cross-partisan" education policies. Unlike traditional bipartisanship—which is now sometimes viewed as capitulation—cross-partisan support transcends party lines to achieve tangible policy goals, even if backed by differing motivations. Because education is primarily a state responsibility, recent state-level successes reveal five key factors necessary for building cross-partisan support:

1. **Easy Communication:** Policies must be simple to understand and appeal to broad values. Examples include aligning reading instruction to the "science of reading" (which gained traction in 15 states) and addressing the teacher shortage through federally funded teacher apprenticeship programs in 16 states.
2. **Responsiveness to Local Context:** Proposals need support from credible local leaders and must address specific community needs. Examples include the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, which helps relocating military spouses transfer teaching licenses across 11 states, and Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs tailored to local workforces in Idaho and North Carolina.
3. **Political Cover:** Policymakers taking risks on new or unpopular policies need protection from constituents, higher officials, or mandates. For instance, teacher testimony provided cover for reading reforms, while a legally mandated deadline provided the Virginia Board of Education cover to pass compromised history standards.
4. **Both Sides Get a Win:** Opposing parties must be able to claim victory for their constituents. In Arkansas, a proposal coupled Democratic-favored teacher pay raises with Republican-favored school choice expansions. Similarly, 43 states have considered civics education bills that allow local control over content, letting both sides claim success.
5. **Media as an Accelerant:** Mainstream and investigative media can rapidly scale awareness and policy adoption, as seen with the *Sold a Story* podcast catalyzing reading legislation and media coverage scaling the "parent empowerment" movement.

Additionally, advocates must understand their political landscape and consider whether parties share a definition of the problem, the level of urgency, whether the policy supports frontline school staff, and how to frame policies as expanding rather than narrowing options. Finally, organizations should avoid mission creep and value signaling, strictly prioritize their top objectives, and remain open to understanding their political opponents' values. Ultimately, meaningful education reform through cross-partisan collaboration remains achievable.

The NVIDIA Ampere architecture introduces the GA10x class of GPUs, including the GA102 (used in the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40) and the GA104 (used in the GeForce RTX 3070). Building upon the previous Turing architecture, the Ampere architecture is up to 1.7x faster in traditional raster graphics, up to 2x faster in ray tracing, and up to 1.9x more power-efficient.

Fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N custom process, a full GA102 GPU features 28.3 billion transistors, seven Graphics Processing Clusters (GPCs), 42 Texture Processing Clusters (TPCs), and 84 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs). In total, it contains 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. 

Key architectural advancements in GA10x GPUs include:
* **2x FP32 Processing:** The GA10x SM supports FP32 operations on both of its primary datapaths (unlike Turing, which limited one datapath to integer operations). This doubles the peak FP32 processing rate to 128 operations per clock per SM.
* **Second-Generation RT Cores:** These cores double the ray/triangle intersection testing throughput compared to Turing and speed up ray-traced motion blur. Enhanced Async Compute capabilities also allow RT Core workloads to run concurrently with either graphics or compute workloads, and the SM can process two compute workloads simultaneously.
* **Third-Generation Tensor Cores:** Each SM contains four Tensor Cores that support new data types like Tensor Float 32 (TF32), which provides up to 5x the training throughput. A new Sparsity feature doubles the throughput of Tensor Core operations over Turing by utilizing fine-grained structured sparsity.
* **Memory and Cache:** The RTX 3090 and 3080 utilize high-speed GDDR6X memory, while the RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6 memory. The GA10x SM features a 33% larger unified L1 data cache/shared memory (128 KB per SM) and double the shared memory bandwidth compared to Turing.
* **ROP Optimizations:** Raster Operators (ROPs) are now integrated directly into the GPCs rather than tied to the memory controller, increasing the full GA102 ROP count to 112 and boosting raster performance.
* **Interconnects and Display:** GA10x introduces PCIe Gen 4 support (doubling bandwidth over PCIe 3.0), third-generation NVLink (allowing two A40, A6000, or RTX 3090 GPUs to connect), HDMI 2.1, and AV1 decode for 8K HDR streaming.

On October 14, the justices will consider whether restitution imposed under the 1996 Mandatory Victims Restitution Act (MVRA) counts as a criminal punishment, which would subject it to the Constitution's ex post facto clause. If the clause applies, Holsey Ellingburg will only have to pay the restitution required when he robbed a bank, avoiding more onerous statutory revisions. Ellingburg points to several criminal aspects of the MVRA: restitution is imposed during criminal sentencing using criminal procedures, victims have little control over the process, non-payment results in summary incarceration, and both the MVRA and the Supreme Court describe restitution as punitive. Because the federal government declines to defend the sentence enhancement, a court-appointed amicus will argue that there is insufficient evidence that Congress considered the awards criminal.

The Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) measures quality of life (QoL) changes in patients undergoing orthognathic surgery for dentofacial deformities. While Arabic versions have been used previously, they lacked formal psychometric evaluation. This study assessed the reliability, validity, and responsiveness of a newly translated Arabic OQLQ in a cohort of Saudi Arabian patients. 

Following an established translation, back-translation, and pilot-testing process, a prospective study was conducted in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between January 2021 and December 2022. The main sample included 74 adult patients (62.2% female, average age 30 years) from a private practice who completed the 22-item OQLQ and satisfaction scales at various treatment stages, including a subgroup of 12 patients who completed it both before and after surgery. Additionally, 15 university hospital patients completed the questionnaire twice over a two-week interval to assess test-retest reliability. 

The Arabic OQLQ demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Test-retest reliability was excellent overall and for three domains (Spearman’s correlation ≥ 0.75), and good for the "awareness of dentofacial deformity" domain (0.601). Construct validity was supported by weak but positive correlations between surgical satisfaction and both overall OQLQ and facial esthetics scores. Additionally, patients reporting better post-surgery appearance had significantly lower overall OQLQ scores (indicating better QoL). 

Responsiveness testing showed significantly lower overall OQLQ scores after surgery compared to before surgery in both the entire cohort (n=74) and the paired subset (n=12). The paired analysis also showed significantly improved post-surgery facial esthetics scores. 

Study limitations included small sample sizes for the test-retest and paired cohorts, the lack of comparison with other validated instruments, no direct comprehension testing, and sampling from a single private practice. Ultimately, the study concludes that this Arabic version of the OQLQ is conceptually equivalent to the English version, reliable, valid, and responsive for future QoL studies in Arabic-speaking populations.

This study evaluated the humoral and cellular immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines (Pfizer BNT162b2 or Moderna mRNA-1273) in 27 rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients treated with methotrexate (MTX), abatacept, or rituximab, compared to 13 healthy controls. Blood samples collected after the second vaccine dose were analyzed for spike (S)-specific antibodies, pseudovirus neutralization, and receptor-binding domain (RBD)-specific B cell and S-specific T cell responses.

All RA treatment cohorts exhibited altered vaccine responses compared to controls:
* **Rituximab:** Patients on this B cell-depleting therapy had almost no detectable anti-S antibodies and showed reduced S-specific CD4+ T cell responses. 
* **Methotrexate (MTX):** MTX-treated patients showed a significantly reduced frequency of S-specific activated CD4+ T cells and a highly reduced proportion of cells co-expressing IL-21, IL-2, and IFNγ. However, their RBD-specific B cell numbers, B cell class-switching, total anti-S antibody levels, and serum neutralization activity were not significantly different from healthy controls.
* **Abatacept:** Abatacept-treated patients had significantly reduced anti-S antibody levels and serum neutralization activity. While total RBD-specific B cell numbers were similar to controls, abatacept reduced B cell activation, impaired memory B cell differentiation, and decreased class-switching to IgG (retaining more naïve and unswitched IgD+ cells). S-specific CD4+ T cells trended lower and showed significantly reduced production of key cytokines IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21, which correlated with lower serum antibody levels. 

Neither patient age nor sample collection timing accounted for the diminished responses. Ultimately, the findings demonstrate that abatacept impairs optimal T cell-B cell collaboration required for generating neutralizing antibodies and memory B cells. Consequently, the study supports temporarily ceasing abatacept treatment during vaccination, when clinically manageable, to improve vaccine-induced protection against SARS-CoV-2.

In November 1977, the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group organized the UK’s first Reclaim the Night marches. Prompted by the unidentified Yorkshire Ripper's murders, advice for women not to walk alone at night, and general harassment, women in Leeds and 11 other areas marched after dark. Though the marches stopped in the early 1990s, they were revived in 2004. Forty years later, these events and global female activists have inspired *The Darkest Corners*. Entrepreneur and angel investor Stephen Pearse outlines the mechanics of running a startup and raising venture capital. Pearse notes that out of ten startups, typically six fail, three yield moderate returns, and one succeeds by making investors at least ten times their money. To return investor money, startups must plan an exit, either by being acquired or going public; however, founders must always tell investors they plan to go public to show commitment. Large companies often acquire startups because startups can develop new technology much faster, driven by employees working for stock. 

To secure funding, founders must cut through the "noise" of thousands of other pitches by inducing greed and keeping their pitch simple. A pitch should be prepared for 20 minutes to allow for interruptions, use pictures, and avoid technical jargon ("geek speak"). Pearse recommends structuring the pitch in the following order:
1. **The Hook:** A bold statement to grab attention within seven seconds.
2. **The Solution and Magic:** The product and the technology behind it.
3. **Business Model, Marketing, and Sales:** A credible strategy to reach customers.
4. **Competition:** Why the product is better, noting that substituting an existing product is easier than creating a new market.
5. **Management:** Introduced only after investors are already excited about the idea.
6. **Financials, Status, and Timeline:** How the money will be spent and prototype progress.
7. **The Offer:** The specific request for money in exchange for company equity.

Instead of focusing on technical features, the pitch must emphasize customer benefits and business "pain points" that either save or make money. The presenter—ideally the founder or CEO—must be passionate, confident, give firm answers, maintain eye contact, and avoid getting dragged into time-wasting "rat holes" by questioning investors. 

Pearse advises raising money at least six months before it is needed, as closing a round takes six months and investors dislike funding companies under duress. Founders should pitch multiple VCs in parallel to create a feeding frenzy and secure a higher valuation. Getting introduced to VCs through a network or an angel investor is the best way to get noticed. When choosing between VC offers, founders should prioritize top-tier firms with strong track records and networks over avoiding equity dilution. 

Finally, startup success requires closely managing cash flow, building a tough and well-rounded team, staying focused, and being willing to pivot based on customer feedback. Speed to market is far more important than intellectual property and patents. Ultimately, success boils down to leadership, which requires passion, confidence, engagement, and a clear call to action.

Mark Cuban stated that President Donald Trump's planned direct-to-consumer prescription drug website, TrumpRx.gov, could be impactful if it forces pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to change their practices. Launching in early 2026, the federally operated platform will sell discounted medications by bypassing PBMs, which manage drug benefits for insurers and often keep manufacturer rebates. This lecture covers proving lower bounds for the predecessor problem, aiming to show that the upper bounds of Van Emde Boas and fusion tries are essentially optimal. It begins with a historical survey of predecessor lower bounds, noting contributions from Ajtai, Miltersen, Beame and Fich, Xiao, Sen, and Patrascu and Thorup. The lecture focuses on Sen's 2003 proof, which applies to static data structures using polynomial space and proves a lower bound that is tight up to a log log factor. 

To establish this, the proof uses the easier "colored predecessor" problem, where elements are colored red or blue, and a query only reports the predecessor's color. This is analyzed in the cell probe model using communication complexity. In this framework, "Alice" is the query algorithm knowing input *x*, and "Bob" is the static data structure memory holding data *y*. Memory word reads correspond to rounds of communication where Alice sends *a* bits and Bob responds with *b* bits.

The proof relies on the "round elimination" lemma, which eliminates the first message in a communication protocol at the cost of slightly increasing the error probability. Because Alice and Bob have asymmetric roles, eliminating messages from Alice to Bob is handled differently than from Bob to Alice. Eliminating an Alice-to-Bob message divides the word size *w* (similar to Van Emde Boas), while eliminating a Bob-to-Alice message divides the problem size *n* (similar to fusion trees). 

By repeatedly alternating and eliminating messages for *t* rounds, the word size and problem size shrink until one bottoms out. If all messages are eliminated while keeping the total error probability below 1/2 (e.g., at most 1/3), a contradiction is reached because zero communication cannot beat a 50% random coin flip. To avoid this contradiction, the number of rounds *t* must be sufficiently large. This yields the symmetric lower bound of omega min(log base *a* of *w*, log base *b* of *n*), which translates to the near-optimal predecessor lower bound for polynomial space.

The Russell 2000 Index, owned by FTSE Russell, is a market-weighted index measuring the performance of approximately 2,000 U.S. small-cap stocks, representing 10% of the overall U.S. market capitalization. Unlike the S&P 500, which rebalances four times a year, the Russell 2000 rebalances once annually on the fourth Friday of June. This reconstitution involves adding, removing, and adjusting stock weights to accurately reflect market capitalization changes in the small-cap universe. Because managers must buy appreciated stocks and sell depreciated ones, the process creates temporary market imbalances.

These imbalances typically cause a rally at the end of June. The Russell 2000 Rebalancing Trading Strategy capitalizes on this abnormal outperformance by buying on the close of the first trading day after June 23rd and selling on the close of the first trading day of July. Backtesting this strategy from 1988 using the ^RUT cash index shows an average gain of 1.34% over an average holding time of six trading days, outperforming any other period of the year. For comparison, the S&P 500 gained an average of 0.85% (or 0.8%) during the same timeframe. Hedging the long Russell 2000 position with an equal short position in the S&P 500 yields a lower average gain of 0.23%, performing poorly for the first 12 years and remaining flattish over the last decade.

This study explores higher education students' perceptions and preferences regarding Online Learning (OL) and Emergency Remote Education (ERE) to inform the design of post-COVID-19 learning experiences. While OL is a planned, flexible process mediated by technology, ERE emerged as a temporary, rapid shift to remote instruction during the COVID-19 pandemic, often lacking sufficient preparation time, resources, and digital literacy among participants. 

Researchers conducted a case study at a private university in Colombia, surveying 88 undergraduate students who had experience in both OL (designed pre-pandemic) and ERE courses. The survey evaluated 14 components—such as content quality, interaction, assessment, and time requirements—on a 1-10 scale, alongside open-ended questions about the modalities' advantages and disadvantages. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the add-on preferential groups (APG) model, a permutation test, and content analysis.

Results indicate that most students (over 70%) held positive perceptions of both modalities, though they generally preferred OL over ERE. OL scored significantly higher in 10 of the 14 evaluated items, with the largest differences favoring OL in time for independent and asynchronous activities, learning assessment strategies, content quality and quantity, and resource availability. Conversely, preferences for student-student interaction were nearly equal between the two modalities, with ERE's synchronous spaces considered slightly more effective for peer interaction.

Content analysis revealed that students appreciated the comfort, flexibility, and effective learning of both modalities. They specifically valued OL for its superior planning, structure, and organization, and ERE for enabling educational continuity during the health crisis and providing direct synchronous contact with instructors. 

Regarding areas for improvement, students noted that ERE suffered from a lack of organization, insufficient instructor mastery of technological tools, and an excessive amount of content. For OL, students suggested improving student-instructor interaction, reducing repetitive activities to increase dynamism, and adding synchronous meetings. 

The authors conclude that while students view both modalities positively, designing better post-pandemic learning environments requires ongoing instructor training in pedagogical and technological competencies, reducing the time required for students to complete activities, promoting peer-to-peer interaction spaces, and implementing flexible, authentic assessment strategies rather than overloading students with evaluations.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives to align teams with company strategy, often through a combined top-down and bottom-up process. However, even leaders sometimes struggle with over-analyzing simple decisions. In contrast, digital laggards often fail to connect high-level outcomes with overall strategy, causing company-wide misalignment. 

A strong data culture aligns organizations vertically by connecting individuals to company goals, and horizontally by enabling efficient inter-functional collaboration. Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central to their business, successfully aligning leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behaviors. Conversely, digital laggards experience misalignment due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient top-down focus. While changing mindsets is the hardest part of digital transformation, laggards can still evolve by incorporating learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement into daily practices.

Based on their culture and technical sophistication, organizations generally begin their data transformation in one of four patterns: "Data novices" (lacking both the necessary culture and systems), "Insight ready" (possessing an risk-accepting culture but lacking advanced analytical capabilities), "Tech enabled" (having the technology and data but lacking an experimental culture), and "Data reliant" (over-relying on data at the expense of critical thinking). Organizations can use these categories to target actions and build a strong data culture.

The NVIDIA Turing GPU architecture introduces several hardware and software advancements designed to improve graphics, Virtual Reality (VR), and rendering performance. 

**Connectivity and VR Enhancements**
Turing GPUs feature hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, an open industry standard that delivers power, display, and data to VR headsets through a single connector. For multi-GPU setups, Turing TU102 and TU104 GPUs replace MIO and PCIe interfaces with second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI data transfers, enabling higher bandwidth and new display topologies. VR performance is further supported by VRWorks Audio (accelerated by RT Cores), Multi-View Rendering, and Variable Rate Shading.

**Real-Time Ray Tracing and Hybrid Rendering**
Previously, real-time rendering relied primarily on rasterization because ray tracing was too computationally intensive for a single GPU. Turing enables real-time ray tracing—simulating physically accurate reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion—by incorporating dedicated RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs alongside NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores offload the Streaming Multiprocessor (SM) by autonomously accelerating Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, running ray tracing 10 times faster than Pascal GPUs. Turing implements a Hybrid Rendering model, which combines rasterization, ray tracing, and AI. Advanced denoising filters also reduce the number of rays required per pixel. To measure hybrid rendering workloads, NVIDIA uses the RTX-OPS metric, which calculates peak operations of Tensor Cores (used 20% of the time), CUDA cores (80%), RT cores (40%), and INT32 pipes (28%).

**AI and Neural Graphics Acceleration (NGX)**
Exclusive to Turing, NVIDIA NGX uses deep neural networks (DNNs) and Tensor Cores to provide AI-based graphics enhancements, managed via GeForce or Quadro Experience applications. Key NGX features include:
*   **Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS):** Trained on 64x supersampled reference images, DLSS renders at a lower input sample count to infer high-quality target resolutions with roughly half the shading work of Temporal Anti-Aliasing (TAA). A DLSS 2X mode is also available.
*   **InPainting:** Removes unwanted image content and synthesizes new content to fill the gap based on real-world image training.
*   **AI Slow-Mo:** Inserts interpolated frames into video streams for smooth slow-motion.
*   **AI Super Rez:** Upscales image or video resolution by 2x, 4x, or 8x by creating new pixels.

**Advanced Shading Technologies**
Turing introduces several new shading capabilities to optimize GPU workloads:
*   **Mesh Shading:** Introduces Task and Mesh Shaders using a cooperative thread model to eliminate CPU draw call bottlenecks, dynamically generate work, and manage levels of detail (LOD).
*   **Variable Rate Shading (VRS):** Allows developers to dynamically adjust shading rates for every 16x16 pixel region, decoupling shading rate from visibility rate. VRS enables Content Adaptive Shading (lowering rates in low-detail areas), Motion Adaptive Shading (lowering rates for moving objects), and Foveated Rendering (lowering rates in the peripheral vision).
*   **Texture Space Shading (TSS):** Computes and stores shading values as texels in a decoupled texture space, allowing visibility and appearance to be sampled independently and shaded texels to be reused across frames or views.
*   **Multi-View Rendering (MVR):** Expands Pascal's Simultaneous Multi-Projection to support up to four views per pass in hardware, processing shared geometry only once.
*   **Resource Management:** Extends DX12 support to Tier 3 bindless Constant Buffer and Unordered Access Views, and Tier 2 resource heaps.

**Turing GPU Specifications and Disclaimers**
The TU104 GPU (used in GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4) features up to 6 GPCs, 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and NVLink support. The TU106 GPU (used in GeForce RTX 2070) features 3 GPCs, 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support. The document concludes with NVIDIA's legal disclaimers, liability limitations, and trademark notices, stating that specifications are provided "as is" without warranties and products are not authorized for life-support or critical equipment.

The author is returning a bill proposing $1,378,450 for over forty harbor and river improvements to the House of Representatives without approval. The author objects because the Constitution does not grant the Federal Government the power—either expressly or incidentally—to fund or construct internal improvements within the States. 

While federal appropriations for coastal navigation safeguards connected to foreign commerce and naval protection have long been accepted, this bill improperly funds local interior projects, creeks, and rivers unconnected to foreign commerce or actual ports of entry. Sanctioning these measures would remove constitutional restraints and consolidate federal power at the expense of the States. 

Furthermore, this system would cause practical evils, including sectional prejudices, legislative disharmony, and wasteful expenditures driven by combined local interests. It is also unjust to States that fund their own improvements or oppose the practice on principle, yet still contribute equally to the common Treasury. Finally, spending over a million dollars on non-urgent objects is unwise while the country is engaged in a foreign war that already requires loans or Treasury notes. Passing the bill would inevitably lead to increasing annual demands on the Treasury, resulting in higher public debt or taxation.

As online and hybrid learning expand in higher education, including within occupational therapy programs, understanding how student personality traits impact online learning outcomes is increasingly important. This systematic review synthesized existing literature on the influence of student personality traits on satisfaction and success in higher education online learning. 

Following Cochrane Collaboration methodology and PRISMA guidelines, researchers searched seven databases for peer-reviewed English studies published between January 2000 and June 2024. Eligible studies examined higher education students in online components, assessed satisfaction (via surveys) and/or success (via grades or completion), and utilized recognized Big Five or Myers-Briggs personality assessments. Out of 848 identified articles, 23 met the inclusion criteria. All 23 studies were classified as level 4 evidence, resulting in a low overall strength of evidence. Notably, none of the studies specifically examined occupational therapy programs. 

The results were synthesized into three main themes:
1. **Interaction between Personality and Online Education:** Across studies examining fully online courses or programs, traits from the Big Five model—specifically conscientiousness, agreeableness, openness, and emotional stability—generally correlated positively with Grade Point Average (GPA), satisfaction, and learning engagement. Conversely, neuroticism typically correlated negatively with GPA, satisfaction, and engagement, though one study found students with higher neuroticism performed better online, and another noted self-efficacy positively mediated neuroticism. Studies using Myers-Briggs assessments found no significant effect of personality on GPA, though personality influenced satisfaction and performance on specific assignment types. Furthermore, introverts generally preferred online classes and email participation, while extraverts preferred face-to-face classes and interactive elements like discussion groups.
2. **Comparing Personality Across Multiple Class Formats:** When comparing different delivery formats (such as online, blended, and face-to-face), high conscientiousness was significantly related to higher grades regardless of the format. Extraverts generally preferred and had higher satisfaction in face-to-face settings, though one study noted they achieved lower grades in that condition. Another study found neurotic students performed better and enjoyed face-to-face settings more, whereas emotionally stable students succeeded across all formats. 
3. **Personality and Student Choice of Class Format:** Students scoring high in conscientiousness, agreeableness, and openness were more likely to enroll in online education, while neurotic students were the least likely to choose online formats. 

Limitations of this review include the low level of evidence (level 4) of all included studies, the lack of standardized satisfaction surveys, the 2000–2024 publication date restriction alongside rapid technological changes, and potential cultural or language differences across the international studies. Future research should move beyond descriptive studies to test specific interventions and specifically investigate occupational therapy education. Ultimately, because personality traits are relatively stable, educators should support diverse learners—particularly extraverted or neurotic students who may struggle online—by fostering self-efficacy and self-regulated learning skills, and by utilizing Universal Design for Learning (UDL) to create flexible, inclusive online environments.

On April 12, 2021, Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K Current Report with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission. The report announces that Microsoft entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications, Inc. for $56.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $19.7 billion, including Nuance's net debt. Microsoft and Nuance representatives will present information regarding this transaction to investors starting April 12, 2021. The filing includes the press release and investor presentation slides as exhibits and is signed by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

According to reports, 91-year-old Queen Elizabeth intends to abdicate the throne to her eldest son, Prince Charles, if she is still alive at 95. Royal Household sources stated that the Queen wants a seamless transition of the Crown. Royal commentator Robert Jobson reported that courtiers confirmed preparations are moving ahead for a transition, potentially involving the Regency Act, which would grant Charles full power to reign while the Queen lives. Clarence House has not commented on the plan. If the Queen abdicates, Charles would become the oldest-ever UK monarch to be crowned, followed in the line of succession by Prince William and Prince George.

During an ongoing government shutdown, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has identified between 4,132 and 4,232 federal employees for layoffs. This follows an OMB memo directing agencies to consider terminating staff in programs inconsistent with the President's priorities. Affected departments include Commerce, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Homeland Security, the Treasury, and Education. 

Labor unions have sued the government to block the cuts, alleging the shutdown is being used improperly to justify unlawful layoffs. Meanwhile, other federal workers remain furloughed or are working without pay. Many employees across various agencies expect further staffing reductions following an earlier wave of mass firings in the spring, expressing concern over their personal finances, reduced paychecks, agency workloads, and the broader economic impact on local businesses. Additionally, there is uncertainty regarding when the shutdown will end and whether Congress will authorize back pay for furloughed workers.

The NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture introduces significant advancements in GPU performance, memory, and I/O capabilities, delivering up to 2x performance improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI compared to previous generations. It features second-generation RT Cores, which double ray/triangle intersection performance and accelerate motion blur, and third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity.

Developed with Micron Technology, the GA10x memory subsystem utilizes new GDDR6X memory. Using PAM4 signaling and Maximum Transition Avoidance (MTA) encoding, GDDR6X achieves data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/sec. It also features Error Detection and Replay (EDR) technology, which retries failed memory transactions during overclocking to prevent system crashes, resulting in plateauing performance instead.

To resolve traditional storage bottlenecks where game decompression consumes numerous CPU cores, NVIDIA introduced RTX IO. Working alongside Microsoft’s DirectStorage API, RTX IO enables GPU-based lossless decompression and rapid asset loading directly from NVMe SSDs to the GPU. This offloads the CPU and accelerates I/O performance by up to 100x compared to traditional hard drives.

Ampere GPUs upgrade display and media capabilities by supporting HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a with DSC 1.2a, enabling 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz. They include a fifth-generation hardware decoder (NVDEC)—making GA10x the first GPUs to support hardware-accelerated AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR—and a seventh-generation hardware encoder (NVENC) that offloads video encoding from the CPU and graphics engine.

Key GPUs based on this architecture include:
*   **NVIDIA A40:** A data center GPU featuring 48GB of memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink), PCIe Gen4, vGPU support, and compatibility with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.
*   **NVIDIA RTX A6000:** A desktop workstation GPU with a GA102 chip, 10,752 CUDA Cores, and 48GB of GDDR6 memory (scalable to 96GB via NVLink).
*   **GeForce RTX 3090:** A consumer card using the GA102 GPU, 10,496 CUDA Cores, and 24GB of GDDR6X memory, delivering 1.5x the speed of the TITAN RTX and supporting 8K HDR gaming.
*   **GeForce RTX 3070:** A card utilizing the GA104 GPU and GDDR6 memory that outperforms the previous generation's GeForce RTX 2080 Ti, though it lacks NVLink. 

Finally, NVIDIA provides these specifications "as is" without warranties, noting that products are not authorized for life-support or military applications, and customers are responsible for testing products for their specific uses.

International tribunals have established that the proper measure of damages for the detention of a vessel is the loss of its use, calculated as the value of its probable catch or interrupted trade during its enforced absence. This rule was applied in cases against the Chilean and Spanish Governments, and was universally adopted by the Bering Sea Commission in adjusting the claims of Canadian sealers against the United States. Specific awards for vessels such as the *Favorite*, the *Alfred Adams*, and the *Triumph* demonstrate that the Commission based its compensation calculations on the estimated earnings of the vessels' probable catches. Additionally, it is an undisputed principle that a government agent cannot rightfully board a friendly nation's peaceful ship on mere suspicion of trespass and forcibly enroll its citizens into public service to navigate a national ship against their will.

While momentum investing works in the long term by following upward trends, the S&P 500 (SPY) exhibits strong mean-reverting behavior in the short term. Mean reversion is the financial concept that asset prices and returns eventually revert to their long-term average. Because of this, the SPY tends to rise the day after it falls (a red day) and fall the day after it rises (a green day). A Python backtest on the SPY—adjusted for dividends and splits—evaluated a strategy of buying after a red day and selling after a green day. The results demonstrated that this red day strategy outperforms both the green day and traditional buy-and-hold strategies, yielding impressive returns, a higher CAGR, better risk-adjusted returns, less time in the market, and a significantly reduced maximum drawdown.

Ofcom has proposed a scheme requiring fixed landline and broadband providers to pay automatic compensation—via cash or bill credit—for slow repairs, delayed new service activations, or missed engineer appointments. Set by Ofcom, these payments could provide up to £185m annually to 2.6 million additional customers without a lengthy claims process. The author supports the proposal, sharing a customer's experience with unresolved broadband faults to highlight the issue, and urges swift implementation. A consultation is open until 5 June, with a final decision expected around the end of the year.

A Vancouver NHL head coach reflects on both the buildup to and the aftermath of the seventh game of the Stanley Cup Finals against Boston. Prior to the game, the coach expressed excitement, confidence in the team's preparation, and support for player Jeff entering the lineup and leader Daniel's belief in the group. Following the game, the coach expressed disappointment over the loss, refusing to blame injuries and instead crediting Boston as the better team due to their strong play, defense in handling rebounds, and tough goaltending.

Coach DeBoer reflects on a Stanley Cup Final game, stating his team started tentatively, made a mistake the opponent capitalized on, and did not deserve to win. However, he notes the team improved as the game progressed, analyzes itself well, and will play better on Saturday night, expecting a strong response similar to when they started behind against Philadelphia and the Rangers. 

DeBoer also discusses the excitement in the New Jersey community, his supportive wife during his recent unemployment, and maintaining a "business as usual" routine without big speeches. He compares the current challenge to facing Lundqvist in the previous round, noting the need to generate traffic and shots without getting frustrated. Additionally, he addresses the impact of team layoffs, the challenge of evaluating the speed and size of the Kings' forwards on tape versus in person, and the advantage of having extensive experience throughout his entire organization, including assistant coach Larry Robinson.

Punith Kumar, 19, ranked first in India and third internationally in the ACCA Chartered Accountant final P2 exam, scoring 83% in corporate reporting. Balancing rigorous studies at the School of Excellence with an internship at IRIS Techsolve, he plans to clear his remaining papers by September and start a company.

The decline was driven by a sharp sell-off in Internet and technology stocks, profit-taking, trade deficit and earnings worries, and global currency fears surrounding Brazil and rumors of Chinese currency devaluation.
